title: Looking back, the editing style of Blink Twice was rather creative.

commenti.body:
Yes it was a deliberate effect as you described to make the audience uneasy and force Frida’s perspective.

Wouldn’t call Blink Twice non-mainstream though. Its made a by a very famous actor in her directorial debut, has a very famous cast, was distributed by Amazon MGM in 3000+ theatres in the US plus an international release. Not sure how you’re qualifying “mainstream” but if a major studio release with star power and full distribution doesn’t count that I’m not sure what even is mainstream in your opinion 

I don’t mean to harsh your vibe - I applaud you choosing a new theme and going to see the movie. Your analysis was also solid - please keep it up! Just confused by the “non-mainstream” term

Anyone have any thoughts on what Channing Tatum was vaping throughout the movie?

How about what he vaped during the climax that made him radically change his behavior in an instant and stop killing people?

Yes! While the script, in my opinion, would have been in need of some serious refinement, it was really cool how the film presents the events in such a subtly disorienting way.

I am certainly looking forward to watching other pics directed by Kravitz in the future.
She put the amnesia perfume inside the vape so that when he vapes it, he loses his memory and whatnot.

I just mean the film that wasn't getting all the big attention compared to the one people were seeing in theatres? Like, the hype during the time I went to see the film was mostly Alien Romulus. That's what I meant.

Yeah, the editing was clever and “breaking the line” is usually frowned upon, but it was disorienting

Another new one by a female director with the best editing I’ve see all year is “it’s what’s inside” on Netflix. Masterclass stuff.

But that's not how it works in the rest of the movie. 

When the girls take the amnesia flower drug, they simply don't remember what they did later. It doesn't cause them to change their behavior in any way. It just blanks their memory of the events that occurred while they were under the influence of it.

Which means that if he were slipped amnesia stuff, he would have kept behaving the exact same and would have kept killing. Instead, his behavior radically changes. The only time we see peoples behavior change like this is when they ingest the snake venom that makes them remember.

Alien Romulus had an $80m budget and was heavily marketed. It’s a continuation of a massively popular beloved film franchise going back to 1979

Blink Twice is a unique horror made for $20m

Apples and Oranges but moth are extremely mainstream

Yeah she showed amazing control and creative structure in this movie. I hope she has an easier time getting more films made because I heard this was a struggle for her. She deserves some attention from a major studio for her next project for sure

>I started this trend where I would go see non-mainstream films playing in the cinema

I hate to break it to you, but you didn't start any trends. People have been doing this for decades. I definitely encourage you to find some indie movie theaters in your town and see what they're showing.

I realize I'm nitpicking but Blink Twice *is* a mainstream thriller. MGM produced and distributed it. Mainstream theaters carried it.

That said, quality editing tells the story in a way that script and acting alone do not. The same goes for cinematography. Contrary to apparent popular opinion cinematography is not about pretty shots or aesthetics, it's about how to relate information (such as a character's internal state, or the relationship between two characters) nonverbally.
I meant that for myself, rather than going for the usual option like Romulus, I'd go for the other option.
His behavior didn't change. He was just disoriented and confused on where he was and what was going on. Like, he lost his memory on the events that led up to holding the knife.
His behavior completely changed in an instant. He was in the middle of killing someone and just stopped on a dime.

BECAUSE HE FORGOT WHY HE WAS KILLING HER! Imagine blink, and suddenly you find yourself holding a knife to one of the girls you were raping and everything burning around you, with no prior knowledge of what happened earlier.
But we know that is not how it works. The movie set up rules for that stuff that you are now ignoring.
